s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end of the tumor
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation noted by the patient's wife
Tumor located on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Microscopic findings include hyperkeratotic lesion and pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures present
Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
Negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains
Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, mitotic figures present

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts, recent growth and crust formation

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Slowly growing eyelid mass, although less likely given the microscopic findings

shortlist.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location on the eyelid, although negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin reduce likelihood

shortlist.label: Actinic keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion, although typically less aggressive and without mitotic figures

shortlist.label: Inverted follicular keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts, although less likely given the neoplastic squamous cells

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location on the eyelid and recent growth, although less likely given the microscopic findings

shortlist.label: Trichoepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Location on the eyelid and hair involvement, although less likely given the neoplastic squamous cells

raw.rationale: The presence of neoplastic squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures, supports the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor's recent growth and crust formation also align with the aggressive nature of this malignancy.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: While keratoacanthoma can present with similar histological features, the absence of a characteristic central crater and the presence of mitotic figures favor squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The microscopic findings of neoplastic squamous cells and pseudohorn cysts do not support basal cell carcinoma, which typically shows basaloid cells and clefting between the tumor and stroma.

rejected.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and the absence of sebaceous gland differentiation argue against sebaceous gland carcinoma.

rejected.label: Actinic keratosis
rejected.why: Actinic keratosis is a precursor lesion that does not typically exhibit the same level of architectural disarray or cytological atypia as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Inverted follicular keratosis
rejected.why: Inverted follicular keratosis is a benign tumor that does not display the malignant features observed in this case, such as mitotic figures and neoplastic squamous cells.

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Merkel cell carcinoma is a highly aggressive tumor with a distinct neuroendocrine differentiation, which is not evident in this case.

rejected.label: Trichoepithelioma
rejected.why: Trichoepithelioma is a benign adnexal tumor that does not exhibit the cytological atypia or malignant features seen in this case.
